title: 2017 YABANCI DİL BİLGİSİ SEVİYE TESPİT SINAVI SONBAHAR DÖNEMİ (2017-YDS SONBAHAR DÖNEMİ) İNGİLİZCE

questions.questionText: 1. Some ethnic minority groups of students within the US, such as African Americans and Hispanic Americans, achieve below the national average of all students; however, one ---- is the high educational achievements demonstrated by Asian American students.
questions.explanation: Cümlede, bazı etnik azınlık gruplarının ulusal ortalamanın altında başarı gösterdiği belirtilmiş, ardından 'however' (ancak) denilerek Asyalı Amerikalı öğrencilerin yüksek eğitim başarılarının buna bir 'istisna' (exception) olduğu vurgulanmıştır.
options: A) aspiration
B) defect
C) exception
D) influence
E) complaint

questions.questionText: 2. Without artificial fertilisers and pesticides, there would not be enough food grown on Earth to satisfy our needs, even with equal ---- of agricultural output.
questions.explanation: Yapay gübreler ve tarım ilaçları olmasaydı, tarımsal üretimin eşit bir 'dağılımı / paylaştırılması' (distribution) olsa bile dünyada ihtiyaçlarımızı karşılayacak kadar yiyecek yetişemeyeceği anlatılmaktadır.
options: A) recognition
B) deterioration
C) distribution
D) fluctuation
E) reduction

questions.questionText: 3. An important reason to re-evaluate how we are raising the next generation grows out of an incredibly exciting discovery about brain development: during adolescence, the brain's potential to change through experience is ----.
questions.explanation: Ergenlik döneminde beynin deneyim yoluyla değişme potansiyelinin son derece yüksek veya 'muazzam' (tremendous) olduğu belirtiliyor; bu durum gelecek nesli nasıl yetiştirdiğimizi yeniden değerlendirmemiz için heyecan verici bir nedendir.
options: A) tremendous
B) frustrating
C) debatable
D) redundant
E) exhausted

questions.questionText: 4. Children and adolescents with attention deficit or hyperactivity disorder frequently experience difficulties in school settings, most ---- in the areas of academic achievement and interpersonal relationships.
questions.explanation: Dikkat eksikliği veya hiperaktivite bozukluğu olan çocukların okul ortamında 'en belirgin şekilde / bilhassa' (most notably) akademik başarı ve kişilerarası ilişkiler alanlarında zorluklar yaşadığı ifade edilmiştir.
options: A) appropriately
B) urgently
C) subtly
D) compulsorily
E) notably

questions.questionText: 5. Children who grow up in two-parent homes where the parents are non-traditional in their own gender roles ---- less gender-stereotypic behaviour than do children whose parents are traditional in their role enactment.
questions.explanation: Cinsiyet rollerinde geleneksel olmayan ebeveynlerin çocuklarının, geleneksel ebeveynlerin çocuklarına kıyasla daha az cinsiyet kalıplarına dayalı davranış 'sergilediği / gösterdiği' (display) belirtilmiştir.
options: A) display
B) alter
C) achieve
D) reject
E) eradicate

questions.questionText: 6. When Columbus sailed west from Spain in 1492 in pursuit of the riches of the Far East, he ---- recent advances in navigation and age-old geographical knowledge.
questions.explanation: Kolomb batıya doğru denize açıldığında, navigasyondaki son gelişmelere ve asırlık coğrafi bilgiye 'dayanmış / onlardan yararlanmıştır' (drew on). 'Draw on' bir şeyi kullanmak, faydalanmak demektir.
options: A) kept off
B) drew on
C) put forward
D) gave away
E) brought about

questions.questionText: 7. In 1517, the Italian physician Girolamo Fracastoro was probably the first person ---- that fossils are animal remains; however, it was not until the 18th century that scientists ---- to realise that fossils can tell us a great deal about the history of living things.
questions.explanation: Fracastoro 'the first person' olduğu için kendisinden sonraki fiil to-infinitive almalıdır ('to suggest'). İkinci boşlukta ise 'it was not until the 18th century that...' kalıbı basit geçmiş zaman (began) gerektirir.
options: A) suggesting / had begun
B) being suggested / were beginning
C) to have suggested / have begun
D) to suggest / began
E) having suggested / were going to begin

questions.questionText: 8. The technological advancements that once made nations prosperous, such as the internal combustion engine, ---- to shatter empires during the First World War, on a scale few people ---- before the outbreak of the war.
questions.explanation: Birinci Dünya Savaşı sırasında imparatorlukları parçalamak için teknolojik gelişmeler 'kullanıldı' (were used - passive past). İkinci kısımda ise savaş çıkmadan önce çok az insanın hayal 'edebileceği/edebilmiş olduğu' ölçekte (could have imagined) kullanıldığı anlamı vardır.
options: A) had been used / should have imagined
B) should have been used / used to imagine
C) would have been used / might have imagined
D) were used / could have imagined
E) must have been used / can imagine

questions.questionText: 9. Tomatoes are so widely consumed that they represent a vehicle ---- beneficial nutrients to those who ---- expensive seasonal berries.
questions.explanation: Domatesler, faydalı besinleri 'tanıtmak / sunmak için' bir araç (a vehicle to introduce) olarak işlev görür. Bu besinler genellikle pahalı meyveleri 'karşılayamayanlara / almaya gücü yetmeyenlere' (cannot afford) sunulur.
options: A) having introduced / would not afford
B) introducing/ could not afford
C) to have introduced / may not afford
D) to introduce / cannot afford
E) being introduced / might not afford

questions.questionText: 10. Early mastery of fire offered many benefits to humankind, including protection ---- wild animals, heat that enabled them to spread ---- cooler regions and the ability to cook food.
questions.explanation: Vahşi hayvanlara 'karşı' koruma anlamında 'protection against' kullanılır. Daha serin bölgelerin 'içine / içlerine doğru' yayılmayı sağlamak ise 'spread into' kalıbı ile karşılanır.
options: A) against / into
B) from / by
C) to / over
D) for / along
E) on / towards

questions.questionText: 11. Anschluss, the political union of Germany and Austria, was specifically prohibited ---- the Versailles Treaty, but was carried out by Hitler in March 1938 ---- any resistance from the victors of the First World War.
questions.explanation: Versay Antlaşması 'kapsamında / altında' yasaklanan (prohibited under) bir durum, Birinci Dünya Savaşı galiplerinden herhangi bir direniş 'olmaksızın' (without) Hitler tarafından gerçekleştirilmiştir.
options: A) across / through
B) under / without
C) for / on
D) from / behind
E) to / about

questions.questionText: 12. Home-grown produce tastes better than grocery store produce ---- it is freshly picked and perfectly ripe, which shines through even when cooked or preserved.
questions.explanation: Evde yetiştirilen ürünlerin market ürünlerinden daha lezzetli olmasının 'nedeni', taze koparılmış ve tam olgunlaşmış olmasıdır. Bu sebep-sonuç ilişkisini 'because' (çünkü) bağlacı verir.
options: A) although
B) whereas
C) whether
D) because
E) unless

questions.questionText: 13. ---- there have been dozens of proposals for gender-neutral third-person pronouns in English over the past two centuries, none has gained acceptance.
questions.explanation: İngilizcede cinsiyetsiz üçüncü tekil şahıs zamirleri için onlarca teklif olmasına 'rağmen' (Even though), hiçbirinin kabul görmediği zıtlığı ifade edilmiştir.
options: A) Now that
B) As long as
C) In case
D) Once
E) Even though

questions.questionText: 14. The story of the cat's domestication is one of mutual appreciation: early farming communities benefited from cats' rodent-catching skills ---- cats won themselves protection and their independence.
questions.explanation: Karşılıklı takdirden (mutual appreciation) bahsediliyor. Erken tarım toplulukları kedilerin kemirgen yakalama yeteneklerinden yararlanır'ken' (while), kediler de kendilerine koruma ve bağımsızlık kazandı. 'While' eş zamanlılık veya karşılaştırma bildirir.
options: A) even if
B) in case
C) as soon as
D) while
E) just as

questions.questionText: 15. Heart disease is the number one killer of both men and women ---- physical and occupational differences.
questions.explanation: Fiziksel ve mesleki farklılıklara 'bakılmaksızın / onlardan bağımsız olarak' (regardless of), kalp hastalığı hem erkeklerin hem de kadınların bir numaralı katilidir.
options: A) in case of
B) in spite of
C) regardless of
D) similar to
E) as well as

questions.questionText: 16. 19th-century scientists fell into a bitter debate as to ---- intelligence lay in anatomy ---- a vital force was responsible for thoughts.
questions.explanation: Zekanın anatomide 'mi' yattığı, 'yoksa' (whether / or) düşüncelerden yaşamsal bir gücün mü sorumlu olduğu üzerine hararetli bir tartışmaya düştüler.
options: A) as / as
B) neither / nor
C) so / that
D) whether / or
E) not only / but also

questions.questionText: 17. In the 1960s, people had greater employment opportunities and a new buying power. (17)---- this growing affluence, music and fashion became mass-market industries and were quick to cater to the demands of the youth market.
questions.explanation: Artan zenginliğin/refahın 'bir sonucu olarak' (As a result of), müzik ve moda kitlesel pazar endüstrileri haline geldi ve gençlik pazarının taleplerini karşılamada hızlı davrandı.
options: A) Instead of
B) Rather than
C) As a result of
D) Contrary to
E) Regardless of

questions.questionText: 18. The growing popularity of television helped to spread popular culture throughout the world, (18)---- new trends could develop rapidly.
questions.explanation: Televizyonun artan popülaritesi popüler kültürün tüm dünyaya yayılmasına yardımcı oldu, 'böylece / bu yüzden' (so) yeni trendler hızla gelişebildi.
options: A) though
B) otherwise
C) instead
D) just as
E) so

questions.questionText: 19. Programmes such as Top of the Pops in the UK and The Ed Sullivan Show in the US could lead people (19)---- considerable attention to pop music.
questions.explanation: 'Lead someone to do something' kalıbı birini bir şey yapmaya yöneltmek anlamına gelir. Burada da insanları pop müziğe ilgi 'göstermeye' (to pay) yöneltmiştir.
options: A) to be paid
B) having paid
C) to have paid
D) to pay
E) being paid

questions.questionText: 20. In 1962, the Beatles emerged from Liverpool's Cavern Club. Their first album Please Please Me became very famous (20)---- the globe within a year.
questions.explanation: Dünya 'çapında / etrafında' meşhur olmak anlamında 'around the globe' edatı kullanılır.
options: A) from
B) around
C) toward
D) into
E) about

questions.questionText: 21. They grew (21)---- popular, sparking such intense devotion in their fans that it became known as 'Beatlemania'.
questions.explanation: Hayranlarında Beatlemania olarak bilinecek kadar yoğun bir bağlılık uyandıran grubun, 'son derece / muazzam derecede' (immensely) popüler olduğu ifade edilmektedir.
options: A) slightly
B) coincidentally
C) steadily
D) equally
E) immensely

questions.questionText: 22. Since ancient times, architecture has been considered the 'mother' of the arts. (22)---- music, painting, and sculpture that exist in a way separate from life, architecture incorporates life.
questions.explanation: Yaşamdan ayrı bir şekilde var olan müzik, resim ve heykelin 'aksine' (As opposed to), mimarinin yaşamı kendi içine dahil ettiği vurgulanıyor.
options: A) As well as
B) By means of
C) As opposed to
D) In terms of
E) Because of

questions.questionText: 23. People and their activities are an (23)---- component of architecture, not merely as spectators to be entertained but as contributors and participants.
questions.explanation: İnsanlar ve aktiviteleri, mimarinin sadece eğlendirilecek izleyiciler olarak değil, katkıda bulunanlar olarak 'vazgeçilmez / zorunlu' (indispensable) bir bileşenidir.
options: A) impoverished
B) immeasurable
C) unreasonable
D) indispensable
E) unintentional

questions.questionText: 24. Painters, sculptors, and composers of music (24)---- about how their viewers or audience never see or hear their art in quite the same way as it was conceived, or that is interpreted or displayed in ways that affect its innate character.
questions.explanation: Ressamların, heykeltraşların ve müzik bestecilerinin eserlerinin tasarlandığı gibi algılanmamasından genel olarak 'şikayet edebilecekleri / etme ihtimalleri' (may complain) ifade ediliyor.
options: A) would have complained
B) may complain
C) should complain
D) must have complained
E) used to complain

questions.questionText: 25. However, they have control (25)---- the essence of their work and that essence is, in a way, tightly sealed within the object...
questions.explanation: Bir şeyin 'üzerinde' kontrole sahip olmak anlamında 'have control over' yapısı kullanılır.
options: A) about
B) over
C) against
D) from
E) with

questions.questionText: 26. ...tightly sealed within the object: the musical score, the covers of a book or the picture frame. (26)----, even the essence of architecture is realised by the people whose activities it influences.
questions.explanation: Önceki cümlede diğer sanat eserlerinin özünün bir kitap kapağına veya tabloya sıkıca mühürlendiği söylenirken, 'Bunun aksine' (On the contrary) mimarinin özünün onu etkileyen insanların etkinlikleriyle gerçekleştirildiği anlatılır.
options: A) Otherwise
B) Unfortunately
C) For instance
D) Therefore
E) On the contrary

questions.questionText: 27. ---- until they are considered ready to switch to English.
questions.explanation: İngilizceye geçmeye hazır oldukları düşünülene kadar (until...), 'Geçiş dönemli iki dilli eğitimde, öğrencilere akademik dersler kendi anadillerinde öğretilir' (In transitional bilingual education, students are taught academic subjects in their native languages). Bu bir dil geçiş sürecidir.
options: A) Around 2.6 million school-aged children throughout the US do not speak English at all
B) It is difficult for bilingual teachers to help their students improve their native language skills in some subjects
C) In transitional bilingual education, students are taught academic subjects in their native languages
D) The language rights of ethnic minorities in the US have been a source of public controversy for decades
E) Most people who are opposed to bilingualism are part of the English-only movement

questions.questionText: 28. Though China began as a small empire centred on the Great Bend of the Yellow River, ----.
questions.explanation: Çin'in Sarı Nehir üzerinde küçük bir imparatorluk olarak başlamasına RAĞMEN (Though), 'zamanla devasa bir coğrafi alanı kapsayacak şekilde genişledi' (it eventually expanded to cover a vast geographical area) diyerek zıtlık ve coğrafi büyüme mantığı tamamlanır.
options: A) almost all of what we know about its culture comes from the wealthy classes
B) the emperor of China, believed to have descended from the gods, was at the top of society
C) it was with the Shang that we see the first definitive written records
D) kings were constantly battling nomadic groups outside of their borders
E) it eventually expanded to cover a vast geographical area

questions.questionText: 29. While scientists are pretty certain that black holes exist, ----.
questions.explanation: Bilim insanları kara deliklerin var olduğundan oldukça emin olsalar da (While), 'bunları doğrudan hiç gözlemlemediler, yakınlarına yaklaşmak bir yana dursun' (they have never observed one directly...).
options: A) they have never observed one directly, let alone gotten in near proximity of one
B) they are defined as areas in space from which nothing can escape
C) it has been long known that the gravity there is intensely strong
D) they can be formed marking the death of a star
E) they use equations to calculate that black holes must evaporate

questions.questionText: 30. Parchment, which was made from the skins of sheep and goats, was widely used in the ancient world; ----.
questions.explanation: Koyun ve keçi derilerinden yapılan parşömen, antik dünyada yaygın olarak kullanılıyordu; '14. yüzyılda kağıt yapımındaki ilerlemelere kadar Avrupa'nın tercih ettiği yazı malzemesiydi' (it was Europe's favoured writing material until...).
options: A) papyrus was another material largely exported to great libraries
B) those made from the skins of newborn animals were called 'vellum'
C) it differs from leather because it is prepared specifically for writing
D) it was Europe's favoured writing material until the 14th -century advances in paper making
E) among the most famous medieval manuscripts written on parchment is the stunning Très Riches Heures of the Duc de Berry

questions.questionText: 31. Although the science of geology as we know it today is a relatively young field, ----.
questions.explanation: Bugün bildiğimiz şekliyle jeoloji bilimi nispeten genç bir alan olmasına RAĞMEN (Although), 'Dünya'nın süreçlerine dair içgörülü gözlemlerin geçmişi eski Yunanlılara kadar uzanır' zıtlığı cümleyi tamamlar.
options: A) it basically refers to the scientific study of rocks and soil
B) it is a vast field, stretching from palaeontology to mineralogy
C) insightful observations of the Earth's processes dates back to the ancient Greeks
D) many geologists think there are some truths that work most of the time
E) many of the processes attached to geology cannot be used for measurement in all situations

questions.questionText: 32. Preventing children's academic failure means developing individuals who are able to contribute to the common good; ----.
questions.explanation: Çocukların akademik başarısızlıklarını önlemek, ortak iyiliğe katkıda bulunabilecek bireyler yetiştirmek anlamına gelir; 'bu yüzden/dolayısıyla (thus), akademik başarısızlığın önlenmesi herhangi bir toplum için öncelikli bir endişe kaynağı olmalıdır'.
options: A) yet, some types of academic failure prevention call for an increased emphasis on arithmetic skills
B) nevertheless, causes of academic failure include socioeconomic and cultural issues
C) accordingly, academic failure has recently come to mean a failure to acquire basic literacy skills
D) on the contrary, a positive family environment is very important in preventing academic failure
E) thus, the prevention of academic failure should be a primary concern for any society

questions.questionText: 33. ----, we regularly leave digital traces of our economic standing when expressing ourselves through posts on social media.
questions.explanation: Sosyal medyadaki paylaşımlarımızla kendimizi ifade ederken ekonomik durumumuza dair dijital izler bırakmamız, 'para çoğumuzun herkesin önünde tartışmaktan kaçındığı bir konu olmasına rağmen' (Although money is a topic that most of us avoid discussing publicly) zıtlığıyla pekişir.
options: A) In order that people can stay away from the negative effects of the Internet
B) Unless we talk about business, politics and non-profit work with others
C) No matter we reveal our own personal information online
D) Although money is a topic that most of us avoid discussing publicly
E) Since more than half of the Internet users stay away from using social media actively

questions.questionText: 34. Early humans had no explanation for the existence of a vast array of substances and their transformations, ----.
questions.explanation: Erken insanların çok sayıda maddenin varlığını ve dönüşümlerini açıklayacak hiçbir şeyleri olmadığı için, 'bu yüzden kimyasal olayları sadece tanrıların eylemlerine atfedebildiler' (so they could only attribute chemical phenomena to the acts of the gods).
options: A) so they could only attribute chemical phenomena to the acts of the gods
B) but the first step to modern chemistry was the recognition of the fact that atoms existed
C) as they were able to observe various materials on Earth and predict their future forms
D) because chemical researchers identified the building blocks of matter in modern times
E) for they could interpret chemical changes between substances in a small amount of time

questions.questionText: 35. ----, the illness can present itself at any stage of life.
questions.explanation: Hastalığın hayatın herhangi bir aşamasında kendini gösterebilmesi (yaştan bağımsızlık), 'gençlerde (ergenlerde) anoreksiyanın yaygınlığı kesinlikle var olmasına rağmen' (While there is certainly a prevalence of anorexia in teenagers) ifadesiyle karşıtlık bağlamında kullanılır.
options: A) As cultural pressures foster both unhealthy dieting and anorexia
B) Even though anorexia is often claimed to overlap with clinical depression
C) While there is certainly a prevalence of anorexia in teenagers
D) If a lack of serotonin has a causal effect on the existence of anorexia
E) Despite the common belief that anorexia is the result of an abnormality in the brain

questions.questionText: 36. World Space Week takes place every year in October, ----.
questions.explanation: Dünya Uzay Haftası her yıl Ekim ayında gerçekleşir 've Birleşmiş Milletler tarafından ilan edilmesinden bu yana dünyadaki en büyük kamusal uzay etkinliği haline gelmiştir'.
options: A) so World Space Week 2016 has been, by far, the largest space celebration in history
B) because you do not have to be an astronaut to be part of the global celebration of World Space Week
C) and it has grown into the largest public space event on Earth since its declaration by the United Nations
D) but it can be a great framework for countries and agencies to foster space exploration
E) while the Mexican Space Agency has been an important promoter of World Space Week

questions.questionText: 37. New Zealand, separated from other land masses, has unique plant and animal species, which are vulnerable to the impacts of non-native species.
questions.explanation: Orijinal cümle 'Diğer kara parçalarından ayrı olan Yeni Zelanda, yabancı türlerin etkilerine karşı savunmasız hâlde bulunan eşsiz bitki ve hayvan türlerine sahiptir' anlamına gelir. 'separated from' (ayrı olan) ve 'which are vulnerable to' (... savunmasız halde bulunan) yapıları D şıkkında eksiksizdir.
options: A) Eşsiz bitki ve hayvan türlerinin bulunduğu Yeni Zelanda diğer kara parçalarından ayrıdır, dolayısıyla bu türler yabancı türlerin etkilerine karşı savunmasızdır.
B) Yeni Zelanda'nın diğer kara parçalarından ayrı olması, eşsiz bitki ve hayvan türlerini yabancı türlerin etkilerine karşı savunmasız hale getirmiştir.
C) Yeni Zelanda diğer kara parçalarından ayrılmış olsa da yabancı türlerin etkilerine karşı savunmasız hâlde bulunan eşsiz bitki ve hayvan türlerine sahiptir.
D) Diğer kara parçalarından ayrı olan Yeni Zelanda, yabancı türlerin etkilerine karşı savunmasız hâlde bulunan eşsiz bitki ve hayvan türlerine sahiptir.
E) Yeni Zelanda diğer kara parçalarından ayrı olduğu için burada bulunan eşsiz bitki ve hayvan türleri, yabancı türlerin etkilerine karşı savunmasızdır.

questions.questionText: 38. Believing that sports could be used to promote peace between countries, the French aristocrat Pierre de Coubertin organised the first modern Olympic Games in Athens, in 1896.
questions.explanation: 'Believing that...' ifadesi '... inanarak' veya 'inancıyla' şeklinde çevrilir. 'Fransız aristokrat Pierre de Coubertin, sporun ülkeler arasındaki barışa önayak olması için kullanılabileceğine inanarak 1896'da Atina'da ilk modern Olimpiyat Oyunları'nı düzenledi' diyen A şıkkı doğru karşılıktır.
options: A) Fransız aristokrat Pierre de Coubertin, sporun ülkeler arasındaki barışa önayak olması için kullanılabileceğine inanarak 1896'da Atina'da ilk modern Olimpiyat Oyunları'nı düzenledi.
B) 1896'da, sporun ülkeler arasındaki barışa önayak olması için kullanılabileceği inancıyla ilk modern Olimpiyat Oyunları'nı düzenleyen kişi Fransız aristokrat Pierre de Coubertin'dir.
C) Fransız aristokrat Pierre de Coubertin, spor aracılığıyla ülkeler arasındaki barışa önayak olunabileceğine inanarak 1896'da Atina'da ilk modern Olimpiyat Oyunları'nı düzenledi.
D) Fransız aristokrat Pierre de Coubertin, sporun ülkeler arasındaki barışa önayak olabileceğine inandığı için 1896'da Atina'da ilk modern Olimpiyat Oyunları'nın düzenlenmesini sağladı.
E) lik modern Olimpiyat Oyunları'nın 1896'da düzenlenmesi, Fransız aristokrat Pierre de Coubertin'in sporun ülkeler arasındaki barışa önayak olması için kullanılabileceği düşüncesine dayanır.

questions.questionText: 39. Originally imported from China in the 12th century, tea has been a significant component of Japanese culture ever since.
questions.explanation: 'Originally imported from China in the 12th century' (Aslında 12. yüzyılda Çin'den getirilen çay), 'tea has been a significant component... ever since' (o zamandan beri Japon kültürünün önemli bir parçası olmuştur). B şıkkı bu yapıları hatasız verir.
options: A) 12. yüzyıldan beri Japon kültürünün önemli bir parçası olan çay, aslında Çin'den getirilmiştir.
B) 12. yüzyılda aslında Çin'den getirilen çay, o zamandan beri Japon kültürünün önemli bir parçası olmuştur.
C) Japon kültürünün önemli bir parçası olan çay, aslında 12. yüzyıldan beri Çin'den getirilmektedir.
D) Çay aslında 12. yüzyılda Çin'den getirilse de o zamandan beri Japon kültürünün önemli bir parçası olmuştur.
E) Çay aslında 12. yüzyılda Çin'den getirildiğinden beri Japon kültürünün önemli bir parçası olmuştur.

questions.questionText: 40. Kutup ayıları iklim değişikliğinin sadece sembolü değil, aynı zamanda her yaz biraz daha seyrekleşen doğal yaşam alanlarını terk eden asıl kurbanlarıdır.
questions.explanation: 'Kutup ayıları iklim değişikliğinin sadece sembolü değil' (Polar bears are not just the symbol of climate change), 'aynı zamanda... asıl kurbanlarıdır' (but they are also true victims), 'terk eden...' (leaving their habitat which has become sparser each summer). D şıkkı cümleyi eksiksiz çevirir.
options: A) Polar bears are both the symbol of climate change and true victims of it, because they have to leave their habitat which has become sparser every summer.
B) Climate change is not only responsible for making polar bears a symbol but also a victim of it, as they have to leave their habitat becoming sparser every summer.
C) Polar bears are known as both the symbol and the victims of climate change since they have to leave their habitat every summer as it becomes sparser.
D) Polar bears are not just the symbol of climate change but they are also true victims, leaving their habitat which has become sparser each summer.
E) Polar bears have become the symbol of climate change; however, they are also the victims of it due to the necessity of leaving their habitat every summer.

questions.questionText: 41. Newton'ın evrensel yer çekimi kanunu, Güneş sistemindeki nesnelerin matematiksel olarak tahmin edilebilir bir dizi kurala göre hareket ettiğini göstermektedir.
questions.explanation: Özne 'Newton's law of universal gravitation', yüklem 'shows that', nesne/yancümle ise 'the objects in the solar system move according to a mathematically predictable set of rules' şeklindedir. B şıkkı tam karşılıktır.
options: A) It is shown by Newton's law of universal gravitation that the objects in the solar system move according to a mathematically predictable set of rules.
B) Newton's law of universal gravitation shows that the objects in the solar system move according to a mathematically predictable set of rules.
C) Newton's law of universal gravitation shows how the objects in the solar system move according to a mathematically predictable set of rules.
D) Thanks to Newton's law of universal gravitation, it is shown that the objects in the solar system move according to a mathematically predictable set of rules.
E) Newton's law of universal gravitation shows that the moves of the objects in the solar system are linked to a mathematically predictable set of rules.

questions.questionText: 42. Besin kaynaklarının dağılımı, bolluğu ve mevsimselliği, insanların göçebe veya yerleşik bir yaşam sürme tercihini etkilemiştir.
questions.explanation: Cümlenin öznesi 'Besin kaynaklarının dağılımı, bolluğu ve mevsimselliği' (The distribution, abundance and seasonality of food resources), fiili 'etkilemiştir' (affected), nesnesi ise 'insanların göçebe veya yerleşik bir yaşam sürme tercihini' (people's choice to live a nomadic or settled existence) şeklindedir.
options: A) The distribution, abundance and seasonality of food resources affected people's choice to live a nomadic or settled existence.
B) What affected people's choice to live a nomadic or settled existence were the distribution, abundance and seasonality of food resources.
C) People's choice to live a nomadic or settled existence was affected by the distribution, abundance and seasonality of food resources.
D) Food resources, with their distribution, abundance and seasonality, affected people's choice to live a nomadic or settled existence.
E) People's choice to live a nomadic or settled existence was affected by food resources, based on their distribution, abundance and seasonality.

questions.questionText: 43. By asking questions such as "Is this water safe to drink?", what is the author actually trying to say?
questions.explanation: Yazar bu soruları sorarak, internetin karşımızda duran spesifik nesneler (örneğin bu su güvenli mi?) hakkında kesin cevaplar veremediğini, yani çevrimiçi aramalarımız aracılığıyla öğrenebileceklerimizin sınırsız olmadığını ('What we can learn through online searches is not endless') vurgulamaya çalışmaktadır.
options: A) We can expand our knowledge about almost everything by using the Internet.
B) A great number of questions can be answered thanks to the Internet.
C) What we can learn through online searches is not endless.
D) Doubtful statements made by others cannot be exactly clarified by doing online searches.
E) We can easily discover averages and tendencies via search engines.

questions.questionText: 44. What is the main function of NIR spectrometers?
questions.explanation: Metinde NIR spektrometrelerinin, nesnelerin içindeki su, şeker, lif gibi belirli maddeleri (chemical make-up) incelememizi ve içlerinde ne olduğunu belirlememizi ('identify what is inside') sağladığı açıklanmaktadır.
options: A) They enable us to examine the chemical structure of objects.
B) They help scientists explore the chemistry of objects through search engines.
C) They reply to questions that cannot be answered through the Internet.
D) They reveal the amount of substances like water and sugar in foods.
E) They detect whether objects are destroyed by X-rays or ultraviolet radiation.

questions.questionText: 45. What is the drawback of NIR spectrometers?
questions.explanation: Parçada, nesnelerin kimyasal yapısını inceleme teknolojisinin var olduğu, ancak bunun laboratuvar ortamındaki 'hareketsiz / sabit' kitlerle ('limited to immovable pieces of lab kit') sınırlı olduğu bir dezavantaj olarak belirtilmiştir.
options: A) The light they give out can be hazardous.
B) When the substances in an object respond in the same way, they cannot be distinguished.
C) Their functions are limited to foods.
D) They are restricted to laboratory use.
E) They cannot accurately analyse the light reflected from objects.

questions.questionText: 46. Which could be the best title for this passage?
questions.explanation: Metin genel olarak, arama motorlarının eksik kaldığı fiziksel nesnelerin (bir elma veya su gibi) içindeki kimyasal yapıyı görmek için NIR spektrometrelerinin nasıl kullanıldığını anlattığı için 'Seeing Inside Things through NIR Spectrometers' (Nesnelerin İçini NIR Spektrometreleriyle Görmek) en iyi başlıktır.
options: A) Advantages and Limitations of Search Engines
B) Are NIR Spectrometers Safe to Use?
C) Can Wavelengths Be Used with Search Engines?
D) Choosing the Best Food to Eat through Scanning
E) Seeing Inside Things through NIR Spectrometers

questions.questionText: 47. It is understood from the passage that the participants in clinical trials ----.
questions.explanation: Metinde 'people want to volunteer but do not know how' (insanların gönüllü olmak istediği ama nasıl katılacaklarını bilmedikleri) ifade edilmektedir. Bu da katılımcıların bir denemeye nasıl dahil olacaklarına dair bilgi eksikliği yaşadıklarını (often lack the knowledge about how to get involved in a trial) gösterir.
options: A) think that their health benefits are expected to yield
B) are concerned about the side effects of drugs
C) experience important problems
D) feel reluctant to be a part of the trials
E) often lack the knowledge about how to get involved in a trial.

questions.questionText: 48. One can conclude from the passage that the problems of volunteer recruitment ----.
questions.explanation: Gönüllü alımı sorunlarının, insanları bilgilendirmek ve hangi denemeye katılacaklarını seçmelerine yardımcı olmak için daha fazla çaba göstererek (by making more effort to inform and help them to choose...) aşılabileceği ('can be brought on board and kept there') anlatılmaktadır.
options: A) have been solved using a strategy called 'over-recruitment'
B) show many differences in each clinical trial
C) are to be ignored in clinical trials
D) can be overcome if volunteers are well informed and guided
E) make up for waste of time.

questions.questionText: 49. It is stated in the passage that the US Food and Drug Administration ----.
questions.explanation: Metnin ilk cümlesinde 2014 yılının ilaç gelişimi için bir dönüm noktası olduğu ve FDA'nın 1996'dan bu yana en yüksek sayı olan 41 yeni farmasötik ilacı (approved 41 new pharmaceuticals, the most since 1996) onayladığı belirtilmiştir.
options: A) became the most profitable institution
B) prevented premature deaths
C) developed drugs in a short time
D) approved a record number of new drugs in 2014
E) reduced the cost of bringing a new compound to the market.

questions.questionText: 50. Which could be the best title for this passage?
questions.explanation: Yazar ilaç geliştirmedeki yüksek maliyetlerin büyük ölçüde gönüllü bulma sorunundan kaynaklandığını ve gönüllü katılımının daha iyi yönetilmesi gerektiğini vurgulayarak 'Gönüllü Katılımını Ciddiye Almanın Zamanı Geldi' (Time to Take Voluntary Participation in Drug Trials Seriously) ana fikrini öne çıkarır.
options: A) The Activities of the US Food and Drug Administration
B) A Variety of Methods of Volunteer Recruitment in Drug Trials
C) Time to Take Voluntary Participation in Drug Trials Seriously
D) The Huge Expense of Drug Development
E) How to Participate in Clinical Trials of Drugs

questions.questionText: 51. Which of the following is certainly true about Socrates?
questions.explanation: Metinde Sokrates'in kendisini ünlü yapan 'ahlaki reform misyonuna' başladığı ('began the mission of moral reform for which he became famous') açıkça belirtilmiştir.
options: A) His initiation of moral reform made him famous in Athenian society.
B) Socrates earned his living by teaching fellow philosophers.
C) Socrates became a soldier to attain a higher social status.
D) Socrates took up stonecutting in his early years and practised it until his execution.
E) One can learn minute details of his whole life because he is a famous philosopher.

questions.questionText: 52. What could be said about the philosophical tradition of Socrates?
questions.explanation: Sokrates'in vaktini Atinalı hemşerileriyle kendisini ilgilendiren çeşitli ahlaki (etik) konuları tartışarak ve onlara 'erdemli ve onurlu olmaları için ilham vermeye' çalışarak geçirdiği ('arguing about various moral subjects... and attempting to inspire them to be virtuous and honourable') ifade ediliyor.
options: A) His ideas fiercely competed with those of Alcibiades and Critias.
B) His philosophical arguments were heartily welcomed by authorities.
C) His main philosophical point of view was to debate the legitimacy of the Athenian democracy.
D) Authorities thought that his prevailing philosophy was in line with religious principles.
E) He discussed ethical issues with the Athenians to foster virtuous and honourable behavior.

questions.questionText: 53. It can be inferred from the passage that Socrates ----.
questions.explanation: Metinde Sokrates'in takipçileri arasında Atina demokrasisini baltalayan (undermined the Athenian democracy) Alcibiades ve Critias'ın da bulunduğu ve 'muhtemelen bu kötü şöhretli bağlantılar (notorious connections) yüzünden' suçlandığı belirtilir.
options: A) had some ill-famed followers who damaged the Athenian democracy.
B) was accused of changing the Athenian democracy.
C) rejected the accusations in his spontaneous speeches to defend himself in court.
D) was successfully defended by his followers.
E) He failed to take appropriate action to reject the accusations against him.

questions.questionText: 54. Which could be the best title for this passage?
questions.explanation: Metin Sokrates'in mesleği ve savaştaki rolü ile başlayıp, ahlaki fikirlerine, felsefi tartışmalarına, suçlanmasına ve nihayetinde savunmasına ve idamına kadar olan süreci anlattığından 'A Life Story of Socrates: From Ideas to Execution' (Sokrates'in Yaşam Öyküsü: Fikirlerden İdama) en kapsamlı başlıktır.
options: A) Achievements of the Distinguished Ancient Philosopher Socrates
B) The Execution of the Leading Greek Philosopher Socrates
C) Unfounded Accusations Against Socrates
D) A Life Story of Socrates: From Ideas to Execution
E) A Soldier Serving as a Philosopher: Socrates

questions.questionText: 55. What could be inferred about the relationship between the media and body image?
questions.explanation: Metinde medya kaynaklarının genellikle kabul edilen ideal vücut tipine (average body image yerine) daha yakın insanları resmettiği ve bunun sonucunda insanların, özellikle de gençlerin 'beden imajı tasvirlerinden aşırı derecede etkilendiği' ('overly influenced by such depictions') belirtilmiştir.
options: A) The body image promoted by the media encourages people to keep up with the latest trends, thus enriching their lives.
B) The way the media presents body image can badly influence how people see their bodies.
C) The media presents an ideal body type in order to improve people's perceptions of their body image.
D) A great majority of people are aware of how the media affects their perception of body image.
E) The ideal body type described by the media is harshly criticised by families since it has a negative impact on their children's self-esteem.

questions.questionText: 56. It is clearly understood from the passage that young people ----.
questions.explanation: Ebeveynleri tarafından görünüşleri vb. hakkında eleştirilen çocukların, benlik saygısının gelişiminde 'olumsuz bir etkiyle karşılaşabilecekleri' ('have a negative effect on the development of self-esteem') açıkça belirtilmiştir.
options: A) may encounter a lack of self-esteem if they face criticism from their parents
B) can disregard the influence of parental behaviour on their perception of body image
C) could get help from their families or peers to improve their perception of body image
D) tend to follow the latest trends to become much more popular among their peers
E) are often forced by their peers to follow popular trends, which either improves or harms their perception of body image

questions.questionText: 57. According to the author, teasing ----.
questions.explanation: Alay edilmenin (teasing), kişinin çok küçük/büyük, zeki/aptal, popüler/popüler olmaması gibi 'bir dizi başka kişisel karakterizasyonla ilgili olabileceği' ('any of a number of other personal characterisations') metinde belirtilmiştir.
options: A) might sometimes be performed by media sources to draw attention to the importance of body image
B) is generally used by people who are not satisfied with their own body image
C) is used as a way to communicate both positive and negative comments
D) is mostly characterised with criticism on wearing outmoded clothes
E) might concern a great variety of issues related with typical personal features

questions.questionText: 58. What is the main idea of the passage?
questions.explanation: Pasaj genelinde beden imajı algısının medya (toplumsal/societal faktörler) ve aile ile akranlar (familial faktörler) gibi çeşitli dış etkilerden etkilendiği anlatılmaktadır.
options: A) Families can improve their children's body image by criticising them and choosing what is good for them.
B) It is no use ignoring peer pressure if you want to build a positive perception of body image.
C) Popular ways of behaving and types of clothing may help young people build a stronger body image.
D) Various familial and societal factors can influence the perception of body image in young people.
E) Families and society should stop trying to shape young people's body image through criticism and teasing.

questions.questionText: 59. Why is Theophrastus called the 'father of botany'?
questions.explanation: Theophrastus'un bitkiler üzerine halen etkili olan ve iyi bilinen 'iki kitabı' ('two well-known books on plants that are still influential') nedeniyle 'botaniğin babası' olarak adlandırıldığı metinde yazılıdır.
options: A) He distinguished botany from zoology and microbiology as a distinct field.
B) He was more successful than Aristotle in identifying and describing plants.
C) He created the first medical uses of botanicals.
D) He wrote two influential books identifying and describing plants.
E) He was the first to classify plant species based on their microscopic properties.

questions.questionText: 60. Which of the following is true about De Materia Medica?
questions.explanation: Dioscorides tarafından yazılan De Materia Medica'nın, bileşik mikroskobun icadına kadar 1.500 yıl boyunca Batı dünyasında ilaçlar konusunda 'rehber kitap olarak kaldığı' ('remained the guidebook on medicines in the Western world for 1,500 years') belirtilmiştir.
options: A) It contained information on which plants are more widely used to make medicines.
B) It continued to be highly influential even after the invention of the compound microscope.
C) It contributed much to the invention of the compound microscope.
D) It was written to contradict previous botanical texts.
E) It remained the guidebook on medicines in the Western world for 1,500 years.

questions.questionText: 61. It can be concluded from the passage that ----.
questions.explanation: Geçmişte hastalıkları tedavi etmek için ilaç yapımı, ardından İrlanda'daki patates hastalığından (potato blight) sonra ekinlerin gelişimi için kullanılması ve günümüzde de 'daha iyi ekinler geliştirmek ve yeni ilaçlar yaratmak' (develop better crops and create new medicines) için çalışılması, botaniğin tarih boyunca tıbbi ve tarımsal ihtiyaçlarla motive edildiğini gösterir.
options: A) The Chinese made much more progress in botany than ancient Greeks.
B) The study of plants has historically been motivated by medical and agricultural needs.
C) 19th century scientists finally discovered a cure for the potato blight.
D) Plant diseases could not be cured until the invention of the compound microscope.
E) Botany was neglected as a science until the 17th century.

questions.questionText: 62. What is the passage mainly about?
questions.explanation: Metin bitkibiliminin (botany) antik Yunanlılardan (Aristo, Theophrastus, Dioscorides), Çinlilere, 17., 19. yüzyıllara ve günümüze kadar nasıl geliştiğini anlattığı için temel konu 'Botanik biliminin tarihi'dir (The history of the study of botany).
options: A) The comparison of the Western and Chinese studies of botany
B) The differences between botany and other fields of biology
C) The contribution of botany to the cultivation of crops
D) The history of the study of botany
E) The medical applications of botany

questions.questionText: 63. Journalist: Could you tell us about your research on heroic Egyptian kings? Anthropologist: We found a skeleton that showed extensive battle trauma. After examining his injuries, we discovered that he had died due to the injuries he got while on a horse. Journalist: ---- Anthropologist: Previously, the Egyptian kings riding into battle could only be seen in paintings and were thought to be just aggressive depictions of the ruling class. This is the first real evidence that points to the kings actually joining their armies in battle.
questions.explanation: Antropoloğun verdiği 'Daha önce kralların savaşa atla gitmesi sadece resimlerde görülürdü ve abartı sanılırdı... bu gerçek bir kanıt' şeklindeki cevap, gazetecinin 'Bu keşif Mısır krallarına dair geleneksel algımızı nasıl etkiler?' (How does this discovery impact our traditional perceptions...) sorusuna mükemmel uymaktadır.
options: A) How does this discovery impact our traditional perceptions of the Egyptian kings?
B) How often did the Egyptian kings fight in battle and get injured?
C) Why is it significant that all the Egyptian kings were on horseback in battle?
D) What made you think that the Egyptian kings were highly respected?
E) Are there any other skeletons of Egyptian kings proving that they were heroic?

questions.questionText: 64. Patient: I don't know if I'll ever overcome this fear. Can you tell me again about this new memory therapy you want to try? Psychologist: Well, I'm going to show you a series of pictures of the thing you're afraid of at 10-minute intervals. Patient: ---- Psychologist: Time is crucial to disrupting the brain's ability to remember your fear. If we increase the time intervals between the pictures, your brain has more time to remember, and that's exactly what we don't want.
questions.explanation: Psikolog fotoğrafları '10 dakikalık aralıklarla' göstereceğini söylüyor. Hastanın sorusundan sonra psikolog 'Zaman, beynin korkunu hatırlama yeteneğini bozmak için çok önemlidir (Time is crucial...)' yanıtını veriyor. O halde hasta aralıkların uzunluğunun önemli olup olmadığını (Are the lengths of the intervals important?) sormuştur.
options: A) Are the lengths of the intervals important?
B) Is there a particular order of pictures?
C) How many times will you show me these pictures?
D) What does memory have to do with my fear?
E) What happens if my fear doesn't go away?

questions.questionText: 65. Ann: There's a very interesting article in this magazine about a scientist, Ella Al-Shamahi, who's a palaeontologist and also performs stand-up comedy about her field. Jane: Science and comedy, how does that work? Ann: ---- Jane: I get it now. She's using comedy to increase interest in her scientific research. Well, she might be on the right path, maybe comedy is the next stage in the evolution of how we present science.
questions.explanation: Jane 'Bilim ve komedi, bu nasıl işliyor?' diyor. Ann bir açıklama yaptıktan sonra Jane 'Şimdi anlıyorum. Komediyi bilimsel araştırmalarına olan ilgiyi artırmak için kullanıyor' sonucuna varıyor. Demek ki Ann, bilimin iletişim sorununu komediyle aşmayı hedeflediğini ('we seem to have a communication problem in science, so she might be using comedy to get to people...') söylemiştir.
options: A) I guess she's using palaeontology to add variety to the topics she's talking about in her performance to be different from the other stand-up performers.
B) I'm not sure, but I can assume that she might have really good time management skills to be able to do research and fulfill other responsibilities as a palaeontologist.
C) Well, when you think about it, we seem to have a communication problem in science, so she might be using comedy to get to people with no enthusiasm about science.
D) The rest of the article says it's an incredible therapy for her as some of the places she researches are quite dark and it's nice to find the funny side in them.
E) If she's really good at it, these shows might even make her famous meaning that she can also continue doing research in her field if she wants to.

questions.questionText: 66. Journalist: You always highlight the importance of keeping a checklist during complex operations. You've also written a book on how to create such checklists. Why do we need them? Surgeon: Well, they're memory aids. They can help you perform well when you're working with many people on a complex procedure which eventually will save lives during surgery. Journalist: ---- Surgeon: A checklist was used during surgical procedures for 8,000 patients in eight hospitals around the world. In every hospital, major complications were reduced by 36 percent and the death rate was lowered by half.
questions.explanation: Cerrah kontrol listelerinin faydalarını istatistiksel veriler (8000 hasta, komplikasyonlarda %36 düşüş, vb.) ile kanıtlıyor. Gazetecinin sorusu 'Kontrol listelerinin gerçekten faydalı olduğuna dair bir kanıtınız / nasıl ikna oldunuz?' yönünde olmalıdır. 'How did you come to the decision that checklists are really beneficial?' (Kontrol listelerinin gerçekten faydalı olduğuna nasıl karar verdiniz?) en uygunudur.
options: A) How did you come to the decision that checklists are really beneficial?
B) How did you manage to create a common checklist to be used in various complications?
C) How exactly can a checklist be used during a surgical procedure?
D) How could you spare enough time to write a book on checklists while working as a surgeon?
E) How did you convince your medical staff to start using a checklist?

questions.questionText: 67. Robert: Can perfectionism or stress be a reason for nail-biting? Carl: This might be true, but I'm not sure one can find reliable research as to why nail-biting is so addictive. Robert: ---- Carl: Anyway, I think it'd be better not to form an opinion on the causes of nail-biting without knowing all the details and scientific facts.
questions.explanation: Carl 'Bunun çok bağımlılık yapıcı nedenlerine dair güvenilir bir araştırma bulabileceğinden emin değilim' dedikten sonra, Robert araştırmaya dayanmayan ama tahmin içeren bir fikir (speculate) yürütmeli ki Carl tekrar 'Her halükarda (Anyway) tüm bilimsel gerçekleri bilmeden fikir yürütmemek (not to form an opinion) daha iyi olur' desin. E şıkkındaki 'We can speculate that it's to do with experiencing high levels of anxiety and fear...' (Yüksek anksiyete, korku veya sabırsızlıkla ilgisi olduğunu speküle edebiliriz/tahmin edebiliriz) bu spekülasyonu sağlar.
options: A) Some experts say childhood nail-biters are less prone to allergies, presumably because they're exposed to more germs.
B) The most common treatment of this addiction, which is also cheap and widely available, is to apply a bitter-tasting nail polish to the nails.
C) I know some other body-focused repetitive behaviours like skin-picking and the urge to pull out hair, and they sometimes coexist with nail-biting.
D) Doctors state that nail-biting does not only lead to harmful effects in fingers, but also mouth and more generally the digestive system.
E) We can speculate that it's to do with experiencing high levels of anxiety and fear, or being too passionate or impatient about things and events.

questions.questionText: 68. The fierce debate among scientists over whether intelligence is inherited or acquired later is yet to be resolved.
questions.explanation: Orijinal cümle 'Bilim insanları arasında zekanın kalıtsal mı olduğu yoksa sonradan mı kazanıldığı konusundaki şiddetli tartışma henüz çözülmedi (is yet to be resolved)' demektedir. D şıkkı, 'İnsanların zekayla doğuştan mı (innately) donatıldığı yoksa bunu daha sonra mı kazandığı, bilim insanları tarafından hala tartışılıyor (is still being fiercely debated)' diyerek aynı anlamı verir.
options: A) Scientists have not still agreed upon how much of intelligence is inherited and how much of it is acquired after birth.
B) Whether people are innately endowed with intelligence or they acquire it at a later time has stimulated an intense debate among scientists.
C) A hot debate over the inheritance of intelligence has yet to be resolved among scientists.
D) Whether people are born with intelligence or they acquire it later is still being fiercely debated by scientists.
E) The debate among scientists over whether intelligence is inherited or acquired later has finally been resolved.

questions.questionText: 69. According to a new study, there are more overfed people in the world today than those who do not have enough food to eat.
questions.explanation: 'Yeni bir çalışmaya göre, bugün dünyada yiyecek yeterli yemeği olmayanlardan daha fazla aşırı beslenmiş (overfed) insan var' anlamındaki cümle, B şıkkında 'Yakın zamanda yapılan bir çalışma (A recent study reveals that), dünya genelinde aşırı beslenmiş insanların sayısının yetersiz beslenenleri (malnourished) geride bıraktığını (outnumber) ortaya koyuyor' şeklinde kusursuz bir eşdeğerlikle ifade edilmiştir.
options: A) A new study shows that there is a significant increase in the number of overfed people worldwide when compared to those who suffer from a lack of food.
B) A recent study reveals that, across the world, overfed people now outnumber those who are malnourished.
C) A current study suggests that, in today's world, the difference between the number of people who do not have enough food and that of those who overeat is slight.
D) The claim that there are as many overfed people as malnourished people in the world today has been proven by a recent study.
E) A new study has found that malnourished people are far greater in number than overfed people in the entire world today.

questions.questionText: 70. It is imperative that women start modifying their risk factors when they are younger in order to reduce the risk of developing heart disease once they are older.
questions.explanation: Orijinal cümlede 'Yaşlandıklarında kalp hastalığına yakalanma risklerini azaltmak için (in order to reduce the risk...) kadınların daha gençken risk faktörlerini değiştirmeye başlamaları zorunludur/elzemdir (It is imperative that...)' denmektedir. D şıkkında 'Kadınlar, yaşlandıklarında kalp hastalığına yakalanma riskini azaltabilmek için genç yaşta risk faktörlerini hemen değiştirmeye başlamalıdır (Women should immediately begin changing...)' ifadesi bu zorunluluk ve amacı tam yansıtır.
options: A) If women immediately begin changing their risk factors when they are still young, they may decrease their risk of developing heart disease in their old ages.
B) Women are recommended to start changing their risk factors at young ages rather than old ages, because this will reduce the risk of developing heart disease.
C) It is extremely important for women to begin changing their risk factors when they are young because it might not be easy to decrease the risk of having heart disease in their old ages.
D) Women should immediately begin changing their risk factors at a young age so that they can decrease the risk of having heart disease in their old ages.
E) It is urgent that women begin changing their risk factors at a young age, otherwise the risk of developing heart disease among old women cannot be decreased.

questions.questionText: 71. It is already known that flowers display their bright colours and use their beautiful scents to lure bees; however, scientists have recently discovered that they use electric fields as well.
questions.explanation: Çiçeklerin parlak renklerini ve güzel kokularını arıları çekmek (lure) için kullandığı zaten biliniyordu; ANCAK bilim insanları son zamanlarda onların elektrik alanlarını da kullandığını keşfetti. E şıkkı, 'Çiçeklerin arıları çekmek için parlak renklerini ve güzel kokularını kullandığı uzun zamandır bilinmesine rağmen (While it has long been known that...), bilim insanları elektrik alanlarını da kullandıklarını yeni keşfettiler' yapısıyla anlamı tam korur.
options: A) Scientists used to believe that flowers avoided using electric fields to attract bees despite utilising their vivid colours and scents, but now they suggest electric fields are also used.
B) It is common knowledge that bees are attracted by flowers' bright colours and beautiful scents, but what draws them to flowers more effectively is the use of electric fields.
C) It has long been known by scientists that the brilliant colours and appealing scents of flowers to attract bees has been aided by the use of electric fields.
D) Scientists have just discovered that the use of electric fields by flowers to attract bees is as effective as the use of bright colours and beautiful scents.
E) While it has long been known that flowers use their brilliant colours and beautiful scents to attract bees, scientists have just discovered their use of electric fields.

questions.questionText: 72. We are terrified of sharks, largely thanks to their reputation as vicious killers. Shark attacks are rare but appear to be rising: There were 98 unprovoked attacks worldwide in 2015, six fatal. There are three particularly notorious species: tiger sharks, great whites, and oceanic whitetips. ---- Recently, scientists have been shedding new light on these enigmatic creatures that are seemingly vital to the seas, and not as scary as you might think.
questions.explanation: Köpekbalıklarının korkunç şöhreti (vicious killers) ve kötü şöhretli üç türünden bahsediliyor. Boşluktan hemen sonra ise bilim insanlarının onların 'denizler için ne kadar hayati olduğu ve sanıldığı kadar korkutucu olmadığı' yönünde (not as scary as you might think) yeni bulgular ortaya çıkardığı (shedding new light) belirtiliyor. O zaman boşluğa, onların okyanus ekolojisindeki yararlı rolüne dikkat çeken 'Öte yandan, köpekbalıklarının okyanus ekolojisinde oynadığı çok önemli rol daha az bilinen bir gerçektir' (On the other hand, a lesser known fact is the crucial role sharks play in ocean ecology) ifadesi (C şıkkı) gelmelidir.
options: A) Tiger sharks are unlikely to attack divers who keep them in sight.
B) Novice divers may come face-to-face with the sharks and see their true nature.
C) On the other hand, a lesser known fact is the crucial role sharks play in ocean ecology.
D) Tiger sharks in the protected waters of the Bahamas are relatively harmless, but they rarely stay in one place for long.
E) Scientists in Australia say that sharks keep fish numbers down and stop them degrading sea grass ecosystems.

questions.questionText: 73. St. Valentine's Day is set aside for lovers and for declarations of love, with these declarations traditionally sent anonymously. ---- Theories put forward generally refer the custom back to Roman times, telling the story of St. Valentine, a Roman priest who assisted the Christian martyrs during the persecutions in the time of Claudius II. St. Valentine was caught and ordered to give up the Christian faith. He refused to do so and was executed on the 14th February 270 AD. In another telling, St. Valentine was executed for the cause of love, after allowing Christian soldiers to marry in spite of a ban on them imposed by Emperor Claudius Gothicus.
questions.explanation: Sevgililer Günü kutlamasının geleneklerinden bahsedildikten sonra 'Öne sürülen teoriler...' (Theories put forward generally refer...) diye devam ediliyor ve farklı rivayetler/hikayeler (telling the story..., In another telling...) sıralanıyor. Boşlukta bu çeşitliliğe geçiş sağlayacak olan 'Birçok gelenekte olduğu gibi, bu kutlamanın kesin kökenleri belirsizdir ve bunu açıklayan çeşitli hikayeler vardır' cümlesi (B şıkkı) en uygun ifadedir.
options: A) St. Valentine is the patron saint of lovers, but he is also associated with a wide variety of other issues.
B) As with many traditions, the exact origins of this celebration are unclear and there are various stories explaining it.
C) This celebration was initially established by Pope Gelasius I in 496 AD to commemorate the life of St. Valentine.
D) The history of St. Valentine's Day is quite simple and well-documented by historians around the world.
E) The custom of sending greeting cards on this day began in the UK in the 19th century.

questions.questionText: 74. There is some indication that children whose access to television is restricted are less likely to be negatively affected by it, even when they do view it. A study has found that children whose parents restrict viewing are less likely to be unnecessarily fearful of the outside world. ---- In other words, children whose parents severely limit access to television may actually become more aggressive, perhaps due to the frustration that results from the deprivation of privileges.
questions.explanation: Önce televizyon izlemesi kısıtlanan çocukların olumsuz etkilenme ihtimalinin daha düşük olduğu söyleniyor. Sonrasında 'Başka bir deyişle (In other words), aileleri televizyonu ciddi şekilde sınırlayan çocuklar aslında ayrıcalıklarından mahrum bırakılmanın verdiği hayal kırıklığıyla daha saldırganlaşabilir' deniyor. Bu durum önceki olumlu durumun aksine, 'aşırı kısıtlamanın ters tepeceği' fikrini doğurur. A şıkkı 'Ancak, çok aşırı seviyelerdeki kısıtlamanın geri tepeceğine (will backfire) dair bazı kanıtlar olduğuna dikkat edilmelidir' diyerek tam bir mantıksal köprü oluşturur.
options: A) It should be noted, however, that there is some evidence that very extreme levels of restriction will backfire.
B) Children with limited access to television are less likely to believe that what they see on television is real.
C) It is possible that the mere presence of parents while viewing makes children feel happy.
D) Children who receive parental restriction are better able to quickly understand the plots of television programmes.
E) Much of the research on the effects of television viewing has focused on children whose parents are more sophisticated consumers of television.

questions.questionText: 75. Beautifully coloured birds, acrobatic monkeys, and noisy insects are just a few of the sights and sounds in a tropical rainforest - the richest plant and animal habitat in the world. Rainforests are found near the Equator where it is wet and warm enough for plants to grow all year round. Most rainforest trees are evergreen, and they produce food and shelter for a vast number of animals. ---- Every year, huge areas are cut down for timber and to make way for pastures and crops.
questions.explanation: Ormanların zenginliği (richest plant and animal habitat), güzelliği, bitki ve hayvanlar için yiyecek ve barınak üretimi anlatıldıktan sonra, bir anda 'Her yıl devasa alanlar kereste ve tarım/hayvancılık alanı açmak için kesiliyor' gibi negatif bir yıkım durumuna geçilmiştir. Bu geçişi, 'Ancak bu zenginliğe rağmen yağmur ormanları son zamanlarda küçülmektedir (shrinking)' ifadesi (D şıkkı) kusursuz bir zıtlık oluşturarak birbirine bağlar.
options: A) Yet, the negative effect of global warming on this rich fauna can be seen.
B) Therefore, people should try hard to protect the variety of species living in rainforests.
C) In other words, the tropical rainforest is home to various plants and animals.
D) However, despite this richness, rainforests have recently been shrinking.
E) Some trees, on the other hand, are used to provide shelter for human beings.

questions.questionText: 76. (I) Images of distant and unknown places have inspired explorers and public for a very long time. (II) The photographs of Yellowstone were the reason why it was selected as America's first national park in 1872. (III) Photographer William Henry Jackson captured the public's imagination and support by confirming the existence of western landmarks in the park. (IV) Half a century later photographer Ansel Adams began his long career of delighting the public with his pictures of parks that many people would never visit. (V) These landmarks which were previously regarded as glorified myths made it easier to attract attention.
questions.explanation: Paragraf II, III ve V. cümlelerde Yellowstone parkı, W.H. Jackson'ın buradaki simge yapıları (western landmarks) fotoğraflaması ve bu simge yapıların (these landmarks) halkın ilgisini çekmesini ardışık bir yapıda anlatmaktadır. IV. cümle 'Yarım asır sonra Ansel Adams' diyerek kronolojik sırayı bozar ve odaklanılan konuyu değiştirir. Zira V. cümlede geçen 'These landmarks', III. cümledeki 'western landmarks'a gönderme yapar, araya giren Ansel Adams cümlesi bu referansı koparır.
options: A) I
B) II
C) III
D) IV
E) V

questions.questionText: 77. (I) Groups perform many tasks, of which making decisions is one of the most important. (II) The course of our lives is largely determined by decisions made by groups: for example, selection committees, juries, parliaments and groups of friends. (III) In addition, many of us spend a significant portion of our working lives making decisions in groups. (IV) Therefore, social psychologists have long been interested in the social processes involved in group decision-making, and in whether groups make better or different decisions than individuals do. (V) Another important dimension of group decision-making is the ability to recall information.
questions.explanation: I, II, III ve IV numaralı cümleler 'grup halinde karar verme (group decision-making)'nin önemi, hayatımıza/iş hayatımıza etkileri ve bu yüzden sosyal psikologların bu sürece olan ilgisi etrafında bir bütündür. Ancak V. cümle, bir anda grup karar vermenin 'bilgiyi hatırlama' (ability to recall information) gibi tamamen farklı, bilişsel bir boyutuna odaklanarak anlatımın genel akışını ve tematik odağını bozmaktadır.
options: A) I
B) II
C) III
D) IV
E) V

questions.questionText: 78. (I) In the North American autumn, Arctic air meets warmer air from the south, creating the perfect conditions for storms. (II) Wind rages around all of the Great Lakes at this time of year, but Lake Erie is the shallowest and contains the least water. (III) The water of Lake Erie is darkened by mud and sand mixed by the strong currents. (IV) This means its waves are typically the biggest as it is more easily influenced by the wind. (V) As the wind blows, the waves start to build a beat, rhythmically sloshing back and forth along the lake's roughly east-west axis, and growing in height as they do.
questions.explanation: Metin genel olarak Kuzey Amerika'da oluşan fırtınaları, rüzgarı (I, II) ve bu rüzgarın Erie Gölü'ndeki etkisini (dalgaların büyümesini - IV, V) anlatmaktadır. II. cümlede gölün sığ olması ve az su barındırması, IV. cümlede 'bu durum onun dalgalarının en büyük olması anlamına gelir' (This means its waves...) şeklinde bağlanmıştır. III. cümle göl suyunun akıntılar nedeniyle çamur ve kumla kararmasını (rengini) anlatarak fırtına/dalga boyutu temasını kesintiye uğratır.
options: A) I
B) II
C) III
D) IV
E) V

questions.questionText: 79. (I) During impression formation, we tend to pay special attention to negative or potentially threatening information. (II) When we come to form an overall impression of the person, that negative information is weighed more heavily. (III) That is, a negative trait affects an impression more than a positive trait, everything else being equal. (IV) For example, in one study, students rated 97 percent of their professors in college favorably despite all the mixed experiences they have had in their college classes. (V) The main explanation for this fact is that negative traits are more unusual and therefore more distinctive.
questions.explanation: Metnin ana konusu (I, II, III ve V. cümleler) insanların izlenim oluştururken potansiyel olarak tehdit edici ve olumsuz bilgilere özel dikkat göstermesi ve olumsuz özelliklerin, olumlu özelliklerden daha fazla ağırlık taşımasıdır. IV. cümlede ise öğrencilerin profesörlerinin %97'sine 'olumlu' (favorably) not vermesi, yukarıda vurgulanan olumsuz bilginin ağırlığı teorisine tamamen zıt, tutarsız ve konu dışı bir örnektir.
options: A) I
B) II
C) III
D) IV
E) V

questions.questionText: 80. (I) The symptoms of senile dementia generally include a decline in memory, learning, attention, and judgement, as well as disorientation and increased difficulties in communication. (II) Alzheimer's disease is the most common cause of senile dementia, accounting for around 70 percent of all cases. (III) Alzheimer's disease often makes it more difficult to think of the right word, for example. (IV) Behavioural manifestations of Alzheimer's disease include a decline in personal hygiene, inappropriate social behaviour, and apparent changes in personality. (V) Wandering and forgetting what one is doing can also become a serious problem, as this can create a genuine danger.
questions.explanation: Paragraf, yaşlılık demansının (senile dementia) semptomlarından ve en büyük nedeni olan Alzheimer'dan (I, II) bahseder. Sonrasında Alzheimer'ın davranışsal dışavurumları (IV - kişisel hijyen kaybı, uygunsuz davranış) ve dolaşma, unutma gibi ciddi problemlere (V) geçer. III. cümle ('Alzheimer hastalığı, örneğin, doğru kelimeyi düşünmeyi genellikle daha da zorlaştırır') basit ve genel bir örnektir. IV ve V. cümlelerin anlattığı klinik ve büyük 'davranışsal / ciddi' bozukluklarla bağlantısı zayıftır ve akışı keser.
options: A) I
B) II
C) III
D) IV
E) V
